name: turbocompressor_similarity_laws
title: Turbocompressor optimal-regime similarity laws
summary: Teaching exercise: reduced mass flow, reduced rotation speed and the two constants of the optimal-regime similarity laws for a turbocompressor designed for 2000 m3/h of air from 1 bar, 20 C to 3 bar at 10000 rpm.

origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 4 (2004-10-12), exercise 5

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solution of MSTH_041012_exercice_7.EES: 13 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001). Largest relative difference 6.02e-04 on cste_1, from the Air specific volume (CoolProp 0.841172 vs EES 0.841425 m3/kg); M_dot, M_r and cste_2 follow at 3.01e-04.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0059 (MSTH_041012_exercice_7.EES, EES 7.210, 13/13); tools/compare_solution.py, no unit conversion (already SI Pa, C, J)
verification.notes: No common variable exceeds rtol=0.001. Largest relative difference 6.02e-04 on cste_1. v_su, M_dot, M_r and cste_2 differ by 3.01e-04 because CoolProp Air gives v_su = 0.841172 m3/kg against the EES stored 0.841425 m3/kg. cste_1 = r_p/M_r^2 scales with v_su squared, so its relative difference is twice that. N, N_r, r_p and the inputs agree. The factor p_su/1E5 inside M_r is the original reduced-flow definition (pressure in bar), not a unit-system conversion.

related_external: thermo_models TM-0060 (MSTH_041012_exercice_7_suite.EES): continuation of the same exercise, cste_1 and cste_2 imposed, optimal speed and flow at 0.9 bar, 50 C and 2.5 bar
